summary: The all-rounder of the Yonex line: easy depth, a plush and arm-friendly response, and enough pop that a compact swing still gets the ball deep. It suits intermediate to advanced baseliners and returning players who like a forgiving frame. The trade-off is control on aggressive swings, where the power can send balls long, and a dampened feel that some find muted. Spin is good, but the VCORE is the spinnier Yonex.

variantNotes.98: Smaller head for more control, less free power.
variantNotes.100L: Lighter and easier to swing, for players who want less mass.
variantNotes.100 Plus: Extra length for leverage and reach, a little harder to time.
variantNotes.110: More forgiveness and power for those who want maximum help.

summary: The most forgiving and power-assisted frame in the VCORE family, built for players who shape the ball with spin and want a more stable base than earlier generations gave. It suits intermediates stepping up and advanced players who want some help. The trade-offs: this is a refinement of the previous model rather than a leap, reviewers found it a little less whippy and comfortable, and its spin is not the best in the 100 class.
feel: solid and connected, slightly firm on mishits

variantNotes.100L: Lower swingweight for a quicker, lighter swing.
variantNotes.100D: Denser 16x20 pattern and more weight for flatter, more controlled hitting.
variantNotes.98: Smaller head with more precision and less forgiveness.

summary: A comfort-first frame with a flexible, plush response and a light swing, aimed at rising intermediates and players who want something kind to the arm. The 16x18 pattern gives usable spin and net clearance, and off-centre hits stay stable. The trade-off is power: it is low to medium, and heavier hitters or competitive players may find it light on penetration. One reviewer preferred the Wilson Clash 100 for power and comfort.

variantNotes.100L: Lighter and easier to swing, best for newer players.
variantNotes.98: Smaller head, even more flex, less power.
